description: Reads CSV text without storing anything and returns every admissible reading of it: each delimiter (comma, semicolon, tab) with each decimal mark that gives a numeric time column and a numeric concentration column, with the columns, the first rows, what was guessed and the checks on the result (time going back, duplicated times). The first reading is recommended. `needs_choice` is true when the file can be read more than one way or the recommended reading has failed checks: the caller should show the readings and let the person choose, then pass the chosen `delimiter` and `decimal_comma` to data.import. Nothing is imported.

title: Preview a CSV before importing it

description: Reads CSV text (header line, one line per row; comma, semicolon or tab; a decimal comma is understood with a semicolon) into a new worksheet. Roles (time, concentration, subject, dose, route, and for an event table event, rate, dur, cmt, mdv, cens, limit, covariate) and units written in the headers, such as `Conc (ng/mL)`, are recognised; `notes` lists what was guessed or ignored. Use `columns` to set a role or a unit explicitly (any number of columns can be `covariate`; every other role is held by one column). A comment line `# caladrius ...` at the top, as the exports of Caladrius write it, is skipped. A table with a subject column holds several subjects, in one of two layouts. In the profile layout (no `event` column) each subject has its observation rows, one dose and its route at time 0. In the event layout (an `event` column: 0 or `obs` for an observation, 1 or `dose` for a dose) each subject has dose rows (amount, time, route, and for an infusion `dur` or `rate`) and observation rows. `nca.run` without `subject` analyses every subject, one result or one error per subject; `fit.run` needs `subject` to name one, or `all` for one independent fit per subject. A subject whose rows fail a check of the data (a time that goes back or is repeated, a dose that varies, a covariate that varies, a record type or a censoring code that is not allowed, a subject with no observation) is refused with the sentence of that check while the other subjects run; a subject with more than one dose row is refused by the NCA and the fit of this version, which analyse a single dose per profile. Declared covariates are copied into each subject's result and used nowhere else.

columns.description: Explicit role or unit for named columns; a null unit clears it.

title: Import a CSV into a new worksheet

description: Columns with role, unit, type, missing count and range; subjects (the labels of the subject column, in order of appearance: a table with several subjects is analysed by `nca.run` for all of them and by `fit.run` with `subject` = all); unit warnings (dose, concentration and time checked together); the derived units (AUC, clearance, volume); and the first rows. `refused` (only when there is one) lists the subjects that an analysis refuses because of the data checks only, each with the code and the sentence of the check; the other subjects run. A subject with more than one dose row is refused by the analysis itself, not by a data check, so it is not listed there; the analysis says so.

description: Runs the NCA on the profiles of a worksheet (one subject, or every subject when `subject` is omitted) and stores the result in an analysis object (new, or `analysis` updated). Each subject gives its parameters by PKNCA name, each a value or `not_calculated` with a reason, or an error saying what to fix; a subject that the data check refused carries the sentence of its check, and the others run. The route and dose come from the arguments or from the route and dose columns. With an event column (a dose row and observation rows per subject) a subject uses its observation rows and its first dose row: amount, time (the time axis starts at the dose, and observation rows before the dose are left out with the reason `before_dose`: they are counted in `n_before_dose` and named in a note), route, and for an infusion the duration from `dur` or `rate`; a `route` or a `dose` in the arguments wins over the file, with a note, and a route column that contradicts an infusion dose row is an error for that subject. A subject with more than one dose row is refused for that subject only. Each result carries the declared covariates of its subject, copied and used nowhere else.

title: Objective at the starting values

description: Weighted least-squares fit (Gauss-Newton with the Levenberg and Hartley modification) of a one-, two- or three-compartment model to the profile of one subject; stores the result in an analysis object. The result has the status (converged or why not), estimates with standard error, CV% and confidence intervals, diagnostics, observed and predicted values, the smooth curve, the trace, and quality flags. A fit that cannot start is an error and stores nothing. A worksheet with several subjects needs `subject` (one label); without it the fit is refused with `subject_required`. `subject` = all fits every subject on its own, with the same model and options and the initial estimates generated per subject (`initial` and `dose`, when given, apply to each; on an event table a `dose` that differs from the dose row wins, with a note): a request that is wrong for every subject (an unknown parameter in `initial`, an option out of its domain) is refused as a whole and stores nothing; the result is a list in `subjects`, one fit per subject in order of appearance, and a subject that cannot be fitted is that subject's result with its error (a subject that the data check refused carries the sentence of its check) while the others run. `all` is not a job: it has no progress and no cancel. If a subject of the worksheet is really labelled `all`, it is that subject that is fitted, and a note in its result says so. For an infusion model (pk1.iv_infusion, pk2.iv_infusion, pk3.iv_infusion) on an event table, `dur` is held at the duration of the subject's dose row unless `options.fixed.dur` or `initial.dur` says otherwise (a note says when the file's duration is not used, also for a model that does not read it from the file). Each result carries the declared covariates of its subject, copied and used nowhere else.

Stale results are saved as such.
title: Save the project

description: The commands executed so far, oldest first, with their parameters and whether they succeeded, the seal of each answer (`seal`: the SHA-256 of the command, its parameters and its answer, and the engine that made it) and, when the program that runs the engine has a clock, the time (`at`). The history is append-only: entries are never changed or removed. Failed commands are recorded too.

Seal.description: The seal of a command: the SHA-256 of its canonical text (the command, the parameters as received and the result, or the code of the error), and where it was made. engine, commit and input are provenance and are not in the hash.

title: List the executed commands

description: Runs the history of a saved project again, from an empty project and with the parameters the history kept, and checks every step against its stored seal. The project is given as the document (`project`) or its JSON text (`text`); with neither, the history of this session is replayed. Nothing of the current project is read or changed. The result lists each step with its stored seal, the seal computed now and its status (`match`; `diverged`; `no_seal` for a project saved before seals, or a command that carries none; `not_replayable` when the parameters were too large to be kept; `blocked` after such a step), the first step that diverges, and whether the project the steps produce is the project stored in the file (`state`). The verdict is `verified` (every sealed step reproduces its seal and the project is the stored one), `diverged`, `incomplete` (some steps could not be run again), `unsealed` (a project saved before seals) or `empty`. A history that cannot be read is the error `history_damaged`.

EngineId.description: An engine: its version, and the git commit it was built from when that was known.

title: Replay a project and check its seals

description: The drawing of a plot analysis, or of one subject of an NCA analysis, as data that any front can draw: panels with their axes, ticks (value and label), range and series, the points a logarithmic axis cannot show with the sentence that says so, the reference lines and the legend. No pixel and no colour: a series has a role (`subject`, `observed`, `predicted`; for an NCA profile `profile`, `lambda_z_used`, `lambda_z_start`, `lambda_z_fit`, `excluded`, `replaced`) and the theme of whoever draws decides how it looks. A logarithmic axis is already in log10 (its range, its ticks and its points), so a front only maps scene units to pixels. For an NCA analysis `subject` names the subject (it may be left out when there is one) and `log` chooses the semi-logarithmic axis (default linear); the lambda z line is drawn from the intercept and lambda z of the answer, with no new estimate. For a plot analysis `log` keeps only the panels of that axis. `status` says whether the analysis is fresh or stale.

A logarithmic axis is in log10: its min, max, tick values and the points are decades; the tick label is the value in the units of the data. A point with `blq` sits at the marker position of the axis. `hidden` lists the points a logarithmic axis cannot show, with the sentence that says so.
